text:
### Observed differences

- Six activities that used to run in every case now run in only about half of the cases: earlier, A33, A35, A36, A37, A38 and A39 each appeared in 100 in 100 traces (about once per trace); in the later window they appear in about 46–47 in 100 traces (A33, A35, A36) and about 56–57 in 100 traces (A37, A38, A39), still at most once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- In the later window these six form two almost mutually exclusive trios: A33, A35 and A36 co-occur in about 46–47 in 100 traces and A37, A38 and A39 in about 55–56 in 100, while any pair across the two trios shares a trace in only about 2–3 in 100 cases; earlier, every pair among the six co-occurred in 100 in 100 traces. [REL013, REL014, REL018, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL015, REL019, REL022]
- The surrounding activities are unchanged: A30 and A31 still appear in every trace in both windows, A30 still runs before the six (e.g., A30 before A33 in about 46 of the 47 traces where both appear) and A31 after them (A33 before A31 in about 46 of 47). [REL001, REL004, REL007, POS001, POS002]
- Ordering inside each trio remains mixed (e.g., A33 before A35 in about 22 and A35 before A33 in about 24 of 100 later traces), whereas the earlier fixed block order — every one of A33/A35/A36 before every one of A37/A38/A39 (A33 before A37 in 100 in 100 traces) — can no longer be observed because the trios rarely share a trace. [REL013, REL018, REL025, REL015]
- Distances shifted as expected for a shorter block: A30 to A37 typically spanned 4–5 steps earlier and 1–3 steps in the later window, and A33 to A31 likewise shrank from 4–5 to 1–3 steps; accordingly A33/A35/A36 now sit relatively later in the trace (mean about 0.68 → 0.73 of trace length) and A37/A38/A39 slightly earlier (about 0.76–0.77 → 0.74). [LAG001, LAG004, POS003, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

A possibility supported by the evidence is that the six-activity block between A30 and A31 is no longer executed in full: in the later window each case runs either the trio A33–A35–A36 (about 47 in 100 cases) or the trio A37–A38–A39 (about 55 in 100 cases) and almost never both, while A30 and A31 remain in every case and keep their places before and after the block — that is, the six activities appear to have become optional, with the two trios behaving as mutually exclusive alternatives. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL015, REL019, REL022, REL025]

The support is direct and consistent: 53 qualifying items stand against roughly 0.55 expected without change, so the volume of flagged behaviour cannot be explained by random re-splits of a stable process; the participation drop and the pairwise co-occurrence pattern show the change directly, all 27 activity-pair relations fit the same two-trio picture, and every item's difference is larger than in about 995 of 1000 random reference splits. Note that these items largely describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. [OCC001, REL001, REL015, REL025, LAG001, POS003]

Limitations: no edge-level successor evidence is present, so where exactly the choice between the trios is made is not observed, and the cross-trio step-distance items rest on only about 4–5 later-window observations (the corresponding pair relations, however, are backed by all 200 traces per window). A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully exclude is systematic filtering or truncation of later-window traces; the clean, internally coherent two-group structure argues against random loss but not against every filtering scenario. [LAG005, LAG006, REL015, REL022]

Other differences: A30's relative position moved later (mean about 0.62 → 0.67 of trace length) and A31's slightly earlier (about 0.82 → 0.80), consistent side effects of the shorter traces rather than independent changes. [POS001, POS002]
